thread:
sophia: Heads up, Escalation from Nimbus Analytics. They reported tail latency regressions after the 01:22 deploy. p95 and p99 jumped and some requests timed out. Ticket: NIM-88.

eli: can you post numbers and which endpoint/model?

sophia: p95 went from ~180ms -> ~760ms, p99 went from ~750ms -> ~3.4s. Endpoint `chat.generate` using model `redwood/vicuna-13b-q4f`. Region us-west-2.

ops-bot: deploy event: runtime v2026-210 deployed @ 01:22, canary completed @ 01:25. Monitoring alert: request_latency_p99 > 1s at 01:28.

anya-oncall: grabbing infra metrics now.

derek: pulling cache telemetry (typo) _pulling cache telemetry_. Noticed a massive rise in `kv_prefix_miss_ratio` aligned with the deploy. Miss ratio 0.06 -> 0.71. Evictions spiked from ~12/s to ~860/s.

infra_lead: any code changes touching cache keys in this rollout?

sophia: The canary included a routing rewrite to support path suffixes for multi-tenant routes. Might be related.

eli: I queried admin stats: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9090/admin/cache/stats | jq` -> output snippet: ```{\n  "prefix_hits": 19802,\n  "prefix_misses": 52312,\n  "evictions_total": 324560,\n  "capacity_bytes": 268435456\n}```

eli: Also logs show dozens of `cache_key_mismatch` warnings with samples like: `/r/chat.generate` vs `/r/chat.generate/?tenant=nimbus`.

derek: oh that explains it. The new router left query strings in the route when building cache keys. So the same logical prefix is split across many distinct keys by tenant query params. That prevents reuse/warmup and causes thrash.

anya-oncall: can we hotfix quickly? Options: revert, deploy a normalization hotpatch, increase cache capacity, or add temporary tenant-aware cache segmentation.

infra_lead: revert is simplest to restore baseline latency now. But we can attempt a targeted hotpatch that strips query params from prefix keys. If it’s a one-line guard we might patch and roll to canary in ~20m. Revert ETA 10m.

sophia: Nimbus needs ETA to respond to customer. If revert, can deliver within 15m. If patch, maybe 35-45m including smoke tests.

support-bot: Nimbus reported they see 12% of requests still hitting >2s, but overall traffic says latency improving after routing was pointed to previous revision.

eli: repro steps for engineers: 1) warm cache for `/r/chat.generate` with no query params: `curl -X POST http://admin:9090/admin/cache/warmup -d '{"prefix":"/r/chat.generate"}'` 2) run alternating requests with and without params: ```hey -n 5000 -c 80 'https://api.redwood/test/v1/chat' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -m POST -d '{"route":"/r/chat.generate?tenant=nimbus","model":"redwood/vicuna-13b-q4f","input":"hello"}'``` 3) watch `prefix_miss_ratio` and `evictions_total` climb. If you run same load with normalized route `'/r/chat.generate'` misses stay low.

infra_lead: quick patch I sketched: in pkg/cache/key.go normalizeRoute: ```go
func normalizeRoute(r string) string {
  // strip trailing slashes and query string
  r = strings.SplitN(r, "?", 2)[0]
  r = strings.TrimSuffix(r, "/")
  return r
}
```

derek: we should also add unit tests + an integration test that alternates `?tenant=` variants to prevent regressions.

anya-oncall: creating alert for high miss ratio: `alerts create --name cache-prefix-thrash --expr "kv_prefix_miss_ratio > 0.4" --for 3m --notify #eng-runtime`

ops-bot: Incident created: NIM-88 (KV/prefix cache thrash causing p95/p99 regressions) by anya-oncall.

infra_lead: decision: roll back the routing rewrite now to get customer stable. After rollback, we will ship normalization change + tests to staging, run synthetic alternating workload for 1h, then promote. Also we'll implement a metric `cache_key_variant_count{prefix="..."}` and a dashboard to track "distinct prefix variants per minute".

sophia: roll back command issued: `kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/runtime --to-revision=v2026-208`

eli: after rollback and pod readiness, I triggered cache warmup and observed miss ratio drop to ~0.08 and p95 back to ~210ms within 7 minutes. p99 falling toward baseline. Customer reported improved UX.

anya-oncall: Please capture the exact reproduction artifacts in the ticket (curl, hey commands, admin outputs) and attach wasm/gzip logs where we captured `cache_key_mismatch` traces.

derek: follow-ups for postmortem: 1) fix cache key construction (normalize query string + trailing slashes) 2) add unit & integration tests 3) add alerting for high distinct prefix variants 4) evaluate segmented LRU for tenant-scoped prefixes to avoid cross-tenant thrash 5) review release checklist to include cache-key-impacting changes.

infra_lead: I will also propose a short-term mitigation: for large routes with high cardinality, mark them as "non-prefixed" to rely on direct keying instead of prefix caching, so we avoid global eviction storms.

sophia: patch PR created: `github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4321` with normalization + tests. Requesting review from derek and eli.

eli: I'll add the new time-series metric in the PR so we can alert on it. Metric query example: `sum by (prefix) (count_distinct(cache_key_variant{prefix=~"/r/.*"}) )`

support-bot: Nimbus updated ticket NIM-88: "thanks, latency improving after rollback, please follow up with root cause fix."

ops-bot: Incident NIM-88 status -> mitigated.

anya-oncall: leaving this thread open until PR merges and we run the canary validation. Closing customer after 24h of stable metrics.

sophia: big thanks all. Documenting timeline and adding the synthetic test harness to the repo so oncall can run a 5-minute repro quickly in future.

ops-bot: Note: auto-created checklists: [rollback done, warmup executed, customer notified, postmortem scheduled].
